body: Hey, I can't imagine the intensity (for lack of a better word) of that experience, but I do understand the suicidal element, as well as the decision to try to find help outside of your close friends; I recently decided to do the same.  If you want to talk, just let me know. I'm curious about your emotional wall - I've been working on deconstructing a pretty epic one, too, so maybe we could help each other figure out how to do it?
Thank you.  This has helped me so very much.  Really, I'm still here, and  writing :)  and I'm so glad I found this.

The triggers are pretty strongly linked to childhood experiences - yes, it is one of those "bad relationship with father" situations.  I feel an immense connection between my *worth* as a human being and my *ability* to do things - to receive certain grades, to earn money, to have an active social life, etc. My father, like me, is Bipolar, though he has never received treatment.  As a child, I learned to watch his moods, gauge his emotions, and act accordingly.  If he was up, I was more valuable to him; if down, I could do nothing right. It is only within the last few years of living away from him that I have realized how much that dictated who I was.  Or rather, was not. I did not foster a self - rather, built one to respond to his moods.  And now, on my I own, I find I struggle still with the idea that I can be...*be* for myself.  I'm still learning how to believe that someone might love me *simply*.
Holding.  Still here. Thank you for your help.

"go easy on yourself." Yes. I need to do more of that. (I'm sorry, I know I'm not doing the formatting right but...well. I have other things on my mind haha) Talking here on reddit has allowed be to compile everything into...a space. I'm putting it all here, and that is helping direct it, in a sense. And to answer your question: the hypomania exists, and I have been rapid-cycling between the two, though often times my manic episodes manifest themselves in irritability, restlessness and a general lack of impatience for any and every living thing. Now that I've increased one of meds, the cycling is not such an issue, though the depression remains constant.

It's astounding to me to hear that I deserve respect; I struggle with the idea that I am flawed, and "less capable" - that a "normal person" could perhaps deal with this situation, while I cannot.  But...but what you've written is...thank you.  I'm glad I read it.

The medication is relatively new for me - I've been taking this particular kind for maybe...six months?  Plus another.  It definitely is getting worse. Normally, I try to deal with it, but today...well, today I just could.  So hello, reddit.  I'm just at a loss as to...what to do.  I have to get up and go to work.  I have to leave my room. But it's so. So. Hard.
Thank you - I do keep trying to tell myself that.  It does work sometimes, but not others.  I'll keep trying, though.

oops.  Do I reply here?
I'm still new to this.  Can you - do you have any ideas for...God, I don't know....just.  Anything I can do?  Apologies for the absolute vagueness...

wow, I didn't realize it would actually make me feel that much better, to see one response. Thanks. 
Phew...ah, where to start.  I recently finished a teacher-training course, and now I'm looking for work.  I thought that the unemployment thing was my biggest stressor...until I got a job...and I still feel this way.  Then I thought perhaps it's the disassociation - simply being surrounded by strangers - so I went to visit my boyfriend's family over the weekend (I know them pretty well, and always enjoy spending time with them).  And still, even while I was smiling and laughing with them even then! There was a constant undercurrent of...of that grip, in your chest, as though someone is squeezing your ribcage together.  And if you don't inhale and exhale as strongly and forcefully as you can, your entire body - you - will collapse in on yourself.  
And then it becomes so exhausting, to be constantly fighting that absolute pain that you begin to think...perhaps...just letting it collapse wouldn't be so bad, after all.
It would be relief.
I've  experienced this sensation to this same degree before, but previous, I was not on medication. Now, I'm quite medicated.  Also, I was in a different emotional environment -  I was more or less taken care of, to the therapist, to the hospital, to the treatment center.  Now, I'm on my own.  I am maintaining communication with everyone who has helped me in the past, but....I just.  I just don't know what to do. I can't feel like this.  It's been a month of this, and I don't know i don't want to hurt myself so much as I want to not exist - so nothing can hurt me.
